references.text: The Lord's anger burned against Israel, and he made them wander in the wilderness for forty years until the entire generation that had done what was evil in the Lord's sight died out.
In the fortieth year Moses spoke to the children of Israel, confirming the forty-year period of wandering in the wilderness.
Describes how the entire generation of fighting men died out during the thirty-eight years from Kadesh-Barnea until they crossed the Zered Brook.
The children of Israel wandered in the wilderness for forty years until all the people of fighting men who had come out of Egypt died because they did not obey the Lord's voice.
God was angry with the wilderness generation for forty years and swore that they would not enter his rest.
Israel was called unfaithful to God in the wilderness, a parallel to the accusation of adultery (zenut) in Numbers 14:33.
Their bodies shall fall in this wilderness - a direct parallel to the promise that their bodies would die in the wilderness.
Ask whom God was angry with for forty years - was it not those who sinned and whose bodies fell in the wilderness?
Stephen's speech refers to the forty years in the wilderness when Moses led the people out.
Paul mentions that God bore with them in the wilderness for about forty years.
